r0.why: Sedimentary rock high in aluminium [1], main source of aluminium and gallium [2], dull and reddish-brown/white/tan [4], 1821 Berthier at Les Baux in Provence [6] all stated.

r1.why: All eight minerals and their roles match [3]; forms of the aluminium component dictating extraction conditions is [23].

r2.why: Tropics [9], lateritization of granite/basalt/shale [10], intense weathering with very good drainage [11], kaolinite dissolving and gibbsite precipitating [12], carbonate bauxite places and concentration of dispersed clays as limestone dissolved [8].

r3.why: 1 to 20 metres [44], near surface with little or no overburden so strip mined [17][45], Guinea then Australia and China [16].

r4.why: Pressure vessel with sodium hydroxide at 150-200 C [21], sodium aluminate and Bayer process [22], filtering, cooling and seeding giving pure gibbsite [25], heating above 1,000 C to Al2O3 [26].

r5.why: Dissolved in molten cryolite at about 960 C [27]; electric current, electrolysis, Hall-Heroult named after American and French discoverers [28].

r6.why: Earlier refining with sodium or potassium in a vacuum [29], complicated and costly materials [30], dearer than gold [31], recycling uses less power and may extend reserves [18].

r7.why: Bulk cargo may liquefy if excessively moist [32], rapid shift, instability and possible sinking [33], MS Bulk Jupiter 2015 suspected [34].
